messages.subject: ** Warning: Invalid or missing covariate. **
parts:
Hi, 

I have been using Distance in R for awhile now (somewhat successfully, thank you for providing so many free resources online!) However I am now encountering a new problem. 

I have been using "vegetation strata" as a covariate, and getting good results. However I just went to re-run my models as I write up my results and am running into a new error: " ** Warning: Invalid or missing covariate. **, it still gives me an AIC etc, just with this new warning.

I have since removed NA/missing lines of data for this covariate, and the models run just fine. However, by removing these lines, I have reduced my dataset somewhat (which is less than ideal as its not huge to begin with). 

I would like to know why it is that this is suddenly happening, as I have never seen this error before (and the dataset was not changed before this happened). And is there any way to circumvent this problem without reducing my dataset? 

Many thanks, 
Lucy

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] ** Warning: Invalid or missing covariate. **
parts:
Good morning Lucy.

Could you provide us with more information on this? What version of the Distance and mrds packages are you using that generated the warning? Did you recently update these packages (CRAN update about three weeks ago)?

Let me understand the biological scenario. You have a model that incorporates vegetation strata (as a factor covariate I presume) in the detection function. However, you have detections for which there is no record of the vegetation strata, correct?  How many detections do you have? How many vegetation strata? How many detections per vegetation strata?

The software might provide you with an AIC score, but it might be the case that the estimates are not maximum likelihood estimates if convergence was not achieved. Have a look at the estimated covariate coefficients and more importantly their standard errors to see if they appear to be unusually large. Those would be the steps I would follow if I saw this warning.

I suspect there is insufficient support in your data to fit this model; i.e. some strata may have few detections. Without seeing your data, that's just a guess. In such situations, you might collapse the strata into fewer levels or not model the effect of the vegetation covariate as pooling robustness ensures unbiased estimates of abundance even when failing to include features that might affect detectability.

parts:
Hi Eric,

Thanks for your quick reply!

To answer your questions, I am using Distance version 1.0.9, and the issue has popped up when I had to switch between my new laptop (where there were no errors for this analysis) and an older laptop. I don’t remember updating any packages, but it seems that there’s a difference between the two (and the former is being repaired, so I can’t switch back). I presume this was an issue all along, I just hadn't had the warning message before the update?

 

Yes, that’s correct, so it’s a primate study (multiple species) and I’m using vegetation strata as a factor covariate. I have 288 detections across 3 study sites (I’ve pooled this data as well as stratified it by site), and I was at least getting the models to run as the bigger (pooled) dataset before. Unfortunately, 56 of 288 observations are without vegetation strata data. I originally had four categories of strata, which I have consolidated into two broader categories (lower and upper strata) in the hope that might help, but there are still a couple of cases where there are less than 10 detections of one of the categories (upper strata) when looking at (stratified) study site level.

 

So, am I right in thinking that the issue is both: 1. having rows of data without a value for the strata covariate and 2. With the stratified datasets where one strata category isn’t well represented (less than ten occurrences)?

 

I’m including the output you mentioned for one of my models to see what you think (this is after collapsing the original 4 categories for strata into 2, but still keeping the lines of data that are missing a value for strata):

Detection function parameters

Scale coefficient(s): 

                     estimate        se

(Intercept)         3.4177687 0.3080195

StrataLower Strata -0.7480261 0.3584839

StrataUpper Strata -0.1233200 0.4132978

 

Please let me know what you think.

Best wishes,

Lucy

parts:
Lucy

I'm somewhat more confused from your second message. I presume you are fitting a half-normal key function to your vegetation covariate model.

When you fit a detection function model with a two-level factor covariate, there should only be two parameters in the model (assuming a half normal key). Here is output from a two-level factor covariate model I built a minute ago


You are showing three estimated parameters, but you say you only have two levels of the strata covariate; something doesn't match up. If you're willing to send your data and code to me off-line I'll have a look and try to understand what model you are fitting
